record.paper_title: Measurement of Energy Spectrum and Elemental Composition of PeV Cosmic Rays: Open Problems and Prospects
record.original_question: Which super-PeVatrons, if any, exist in the Inner Galaxy and Galactic Center regions, and what wide-field Southern Hemisphere observations are needed to monitor those regions and test whether they contain sources accelerating particles well beyond PeV energies?

evidence.quote: The observation of sources emitting photons above the PeV in the North suggests the need of a wide field of view instrument in the Southern Hemisphere to monitor the Inner Galaxy and the Galactic Center looking for super-PeVatrons (SWGO [77], STACEX [78]) to operate with CTA-South [79].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A "PeVatron" is an astrophysical source capable of accelerating charged particles (typically protons or nuclei) to energies of at least 1 PeV (10^15 eV); a "super-PeVatron" is a source that accelerates particles to energies well above 1 PeV, and is typically identified via the detection of gamma-ray emission with photon energies exceeding ~100 TeV up to the PeV range. The Inner Galaxy is the region of the Milky Way within roughly ±30° of Galactic longitude around the Galactic Center (Galactic latitude |b| ≲ a few degrees), and the Galactic Center region refers to the central few hundred parsecs surrounding Sagittarius A*. These regions are best observed from the Southern Hemisphere.

Problem. Determine, by means of wide field-of-view ground-based gamma-ray observations of the Inner Galaxy and the Galactic Center conducted from a Southern Hemisphere site:
(a) which (if any) astrophysical sources in these regions are super-PeVatrons, i.e. emit gamma rays with energies substantially above 1 PeV indicating hadronic acceleration well beyond PeV energies;
(b) the instrumental requirements (effective area, angular resolution, gamma/hadron discrimination, duty cycle, sky coverage, and energy threshold/reach) for a wide field-of-view Southern Hemisphere survey instrument that would be sufficient to continuously monitor the Inner Galaxy and the Galactic Center and to confirm or exclude the presence of such super-PeVatrons.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, no source in the Inner Galaxy or Galactic Center has been firmly established as a super-PeVatron emitting gamma rays well above 1 PeV; the Galactic Center has been identified by H.E.S.S. as a likely PeVatron candidate, but conclusive identification of super-PeVatrons requires next-generation Southern Hemisphere wide field-of-view observatories such as SWGO (under construction/planning) together with CTA-South. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: SWGO Collaboration — Science Case
status_evidence.snippet: SWGO is a planned wide field-of-view gamma-ray observatory in the Southern Hemisphere designed to survey the Galactic plane and Galactic Center for PeVatron sources.
status_evidence.claim: A dedicated Southern Hemisphere wide-FoV instrument to search for super-PeVatrons is still under development, indicating the question is open.

status_evidence.title: H.E.S.S. observations of the Galactic Centre PeVatron
status_evidence.snippet: Evidence is presented for a cosmic-ray accelerator at the Galactic Centre reaching PeV energies, but the maximum energy and identification as a super-PeVatron remain uncertain.
status_evidence.claim: Galactic Center is a PeVatron candidate but super-PeVatron status is not established.
